planning_2b.question: Which way of carrying state across fresh sessions (context loss forced by a 30-turn cap, at most 8 sessions) finishes the task with the fewest sessions or least cost: repository state files (A), the native task list (B), or the same prompt every session with no state instruction (C, the Ralph-style loop)?

arms.B: native task list, one list id per run
arms.C: the same prompt every session, no state instruction

decision.rule: B or C replaces A only when it passes at least as many runs as A and uses fewer sessions or less cost in a majority of the counted fixture-trial cells, with no more lost-work events than A; a cell counts when at least one of the two compared runs passes the hidden tests

primary_design_cap_12.verdict: primary design infeasible (eight sessions of twelve turns is 96 turns before any re-reading; calibration: single sessions needed 40 to 93 turns)

orchestration_1.question: On bounded north-star coding fixes, which orchestration produces the best code for its cost: one session (A), a Workflow pairing the implementer with an adversarial verifier (B), or an interactive agent team (C)?

routing_5.question: Can review micros (one pull-request head, the repository's own brief) move from Opus 5.5 to Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort without losing the known findings, at no more than 60% of Opus's cost?

design.fence: --tools Bash,Read,Glob,Grep with dontAsk and no allow rule; the home tree and each other run's directory denied by name; the network closed; the brief alone, no gate records or CI state
design.ground_truth: 22 findings known from earlier Opus and GPT reads, 12 of them decisive (reachable from the pull request, its commits, its description and an offline sandbox)
design.judging: a blind first judge and a refuter, both claude-opus-5-5 at max effort on stripped packets (order fixed by a hash of head and trial, the refuter given the pair swapped)
design.rule: Sonnet takes review micros only if, for every decisive finding, it found the finding in at least as many of its runs as Opus did, and the cost of its runs (the counter, main and subagent sources) is at most 60% of Opus's; otherwise Opus stays
design.second_trial: run as an extension the command center decided after trial 1; the rule is applied to detection frequencies over the two trials

findings.title: README-overnight claims no command starts a trial the transport would then refuse; a boats feed is accepted at config load and refused only after the trial starts, leaving a stuck state
The weekly systemd unit's PATH does not contain gh, and the fetch does not catch FileNotFoundError, so every weekly run exits 1

The new routing skill has no grant in the reviewed architecture inventory: test_local_pages_policy_grants fails

The 'bundled claude-api skill' duplicate reason is dropped from manifest.json:883 without evidence

The closeout loader does not refuse an installed jsonschema version other than the pinned 4.26.0

superseded.reason: incomplete by the preregistered rule: it covered every known id and agreed with the first judge on all 22 cells but listed three P3 findings as unmatched

decision.two_trial_verdict_basis: a ruled extension: trial 1 met the registered rule (Sonnet takes review micros); the rule for two trials was fixed before any run (addendum 1) and so was its trigger, which ends the run after a passing trial 1 (Sonnet takes review micros, no second trial); the command center ran trial 2 after seeing that result (addendum 3 of the run's papers), so the two-trial verdict is not a preregistered outcome, and an extension after a pass can only move the verdict toward Opus

tolerant_floor_basis.reading_and_null_model: the run's own, registered before any run: papers.addendum_01, lines 17-18 (the tolerant reading, and the noise floors of two identical reviewers who each find a finding with probability p in each run); no third-party source defines this registered reading, so the reference is the brute-force enumeration in tests/test_paired_runs_results.py
tolerant_floor_basis.sum_of_independent_differences: numpy 2.5.3, numpy.convolve documentation: the sum of two independent random variables is distributed according to the convolution of their individual distributions; the test cross-checks tolerant_floor against numpy.convolve where numpy is installed

exposure.outside_data: no flagged call returned data about the pull request, the records, the other runs or the known findings; one run received environment information only (a directory name and its PATH)
exposure.limit: the client's persisted tool outputs sit in a directory the fence denies; runs that tried to read them were refused (3 Opus runs in trial 2, 2 in trial 1)

ruling.decision: the strict reading stands, so Opus stays the default for Claude review micros
ruling.routing: Opus for every Claude read or micro of trading code and gate code, and for any micro that is the only Claude-family read of a gate; Sonnet at medium only for non-gate foundation changes (docs, pages, catalogs, generated reports) where the change is mechanical or a second Claude-family read exists; no slot row, default or skill text changes from the ruling alone
